subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should third-party plugin manifests be allowed to alter user configuration during installation, and if so which keys, consent mechanism, and rollback/provenance guarantees form the supported contract?
rationale: This choice establishes a compatibility- and security-sensitive plugin API with user-settings authority; source inspection cannot determine the intended trust and consent policy.

options.title: Adopt constrained config intents
options.body: Define an allowlisted, declarative install-time intent API with reviewed diff/skip UX, validation, conflict semantics, and recorded provenance.

options.title: Keep setup explicit
options.body: Continue requiring plugins to document or run explicit setup flows instead of permitting manifest-driven configuration mutation.

options.title: Defer pending config policy
options.body: Resolve the broader configuration pre-apply policy before adding any install-time plugin mutation contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt constrained config intents
recommendation.body: Define an allowlisted, declarative install-time intent API with reviewed diff/skip UX, validation, conflict semantics, and recorded provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest substantive review already identifies this as a maintainer-owned product/security decision on the plugin manifest and installation boundary.
